I almost drowned in Lake Huron when I was teenager. It was stormy and there was a severe undertow that day. I was a decent swimmer and wanted to enjoy the big waves. I went in maybe 20 feet at first but then the water took me further. At that point I was at the mercy of the waves. I tried to swim parallel to the shore like you are supposed to, but the waves kept launching me closer and closer to this metal break-wall that extended perpendicular from the shore. There was seemingly no way I wasn't going to be launched right into this metal wall. The last wave before impact, I purposely covered my head as much as I could with both arms, thinking that if I hit my head against the wall, I could easily lose consciousness or be dazed and would surely die. Well, by the grace of God (or science) I didn't hit the wall at all. I ended up downstream of the primary wave direction and was able to swim to shore. My legs felt like jello for hours afterward. To this day, I have no idea how I didn't hit the wall. My palms get sweaty thinking about it all these years later.
